plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero.
This significantly reduces overall portfolio risk and leverage.
Focus on capital preservation with broad index and income holdings.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest returns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to comply with the single-name mandate.
Reduce exposure to all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to smaller allocations.
This lowers overall leverage while maintaining some growth potential.
Buy XLV, a strong scanner long setup, to diversify and add quality exposure.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5% per month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality new setup. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, balancing growth with risk management.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Increase exposure to all existing leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to 6% each.
This strategy leans into higher-beta, leveraged positions for aggressive growth.
Buy XLV, a strong scanner long setup, to further capitalize on market opportunities.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets stretch growth, aiming for ~4% per month. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this raises both upside and drawdown potential, and leveraged ETFs experience daily decay/rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage higher risk.

plan: Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income generation.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero.
This shifts the portfolio focus heavily towards income and capital preservation.
Prioritize steady monthly distributions over growth potential.
income.read: This income plan aims to park cash for yield, targeting ~1% per month. It prioritizes steady monthly distributions by increasing income-generating ETFs and eliminating leveraged, high-beta holdings. While focused on income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in market downturns.
